structured_output.scope_summary: EIP-7981, at the assessed revision, adds a per-byte data charge to the intrinsic gas of transactions that carry an access list. The charge is 40 gas for each non-zero byte and 10 gas for each zero byte, counted across all 20-byte addresses and 32-byte storage keys. It is added on top of the existing EIP-2930 per-address cost (2400) and per-storage-key cost (1900). The reference implementation applies it to access-list, fee-market, blob and set-code transactions and leaves the EIP-7623 calldata floor value unchanged. The stated goal is to stop access lists being used to get around EIP-7623 floor pricing and to reduce maximum block size.

evidence.summary: The access-list intrinsic cost becomes the existing per-item cost plus 40 or 10 gas per access-list byte.
The data cost is added to the existing intrinsic gas sum. The floor value is returned unchanged.

evm_gas_rule_changes.rationale: An existing intrinsic-gas rule changes: the access-list cost gains a per-byte term. Per-byte data pricing is an existing pattern from calldata. No new kind of metering or settlement is added, so this is level 1.
evm_gas_rule_changes.uncertainty_note: Byte counting over access-list contents could be read as a new accounting mechanism. Because it also changes baseline gas results, that reading would give level 3.

evidence.summary: Only intrinsic gas pricing changes. Warm-loading of access-list entries and opcode behavior are untouched.

state_access_ordering_within_opcode_exec.rationale: No instruction's state-access or gas-charge ordering changes.

evidence.summary: Blob transactions are only affected through their access list's intrinsic cost. Blob gas is not touched.
The change is a data-footprint charge on transaction bytes, not on state writes.
No refund is introduced.

new_evm_gas_refund.rationale: No new refund mechanism is introduced.

evidence.summary: Every typed transaction with a non-empty access list gets a higher intrinsic cost.
A normal access list costs 54.2% more, so expected gas and balances change.

Empty access lists are unaffected, so there is no common rewrite across all families. This is level 2.

unspecified_behavior_requiring_cross_cli.rationale: Whether access-list bytes contribute to EIP-7623 floor tokens is not stated in prose. However, the formula and the reference implementation support one outcome: they are added only to intrinsic gas. Duplicate entries are charged per occurrence by the loop. This is a localized omission with one intended outcome, so level 1.
unspecified_behavior_requiring_cross_cli.uncertainty_note: The Case 3 wording could be read as implying a floor interaction. If that reading competed normatively, this would be level 2.

evidence.summary: The EIP is explicitly designed around EIP-7623 floor pricing.
Gas used is the maximum of the standard cost plus execution and the floor. The higher intrinsic cost changes which side applies.
The per-item costs and duplicate handling that EIP-7981 adds to.

cross_eip_interactions.rationale: Coordinated cases are needed with EIP-7623, for transactions that combine calldata and access lists near the crossover between the floor and the standard cost, and at the validity threshold. EIP-2930 access-list behavior needs compatibility checks: duplicates and warm-set effects are unchanged, and only the charge changes. This is level 2.
cross_eip_interactions.uncertainty_note: Interactions with the blob and set-code transaction types are implied by the reference implementation but not supported by supplied EIP documents.

interacting_eips.coordinated_cases: Transactions combining calldata with access lists: check that gas used equals the maximum of (21000 + calldata standard cost + access-list cost + execution) and the floor. Cover cases on both sides of the crossover. Check that the floor tokens exclude access-list bytes. Check the validity threshold: a gas limit exactly at the maximum of intrinsic gas and the floor versus one below, when access-list data cost dominates.
Duplicate addresses or keys are charged per occurrence, including the data cost. Zero versus non-zero byte composition of addresses and keys is priced correctly. Warm-set preloading is unchanged.

unidentified_interactions: The reference implementation applies the data cost to FeeMarketTransaction, BlobTransaction and SetCodeTransaction access lists. Each of these transaction types needs an intrinsic-gas check, but their defining EIPs are not supplied.

under_specification.summary: Only one minor gap exists. The prose does not state whether access-list bytes count toward EIP-7623 floor tokens. Case 3's wording is vague, but the formula and the reference implementation imply they do not.
unresolved_questions: Do access-list bytes contribute to tokens_in_calldata for the EIP-7623 floor? The reference implementation implies no.

notable_ambiguities: Case 3 says calldata is 'Applied through EIP-7623 mechanism', but it does not say how the access-list data cost relates to the floor.
Whether the per-byte access-list charge is a new accounting mechanism or a changed parameter of the existing intrinsic-gas rule affects the GAS level (1 versus 3).
